Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, with Syed Mokaddus Ali, Advocates  ----- For the Appellants. 
Mahmudul Islam with Probir Neogi and Ramzan Ali Sikder, Advocates.  ----- For Respondent No.1
parties:
Abul Kalam Engineer and another ----- Appellants
Vs.
M Nasiruddin Howlader and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
10. The plaint case, in brief, is that one Anar Ali was original owner in possession of the entire 34 decimals of land of RS Plot No. 1702 appertained to RS Khatian No. 223. After his death, when one of his sons Kala Miah was in exclusive possession of said land, 11 decimals of land was acquired for the Nasirabad Government High School in LA case No. 128/63-64. Then, by two registered deeds being No. 6511 and 6512 dated 28-6-74 Kala Miah transferred rest of 23 decimals of land along with some excess land to defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and delivered possession. Said defendants got the land mutated in their names in mutation case No. 667(1) 1974-75 and got PS Mutation Khatian No. 426/1. BS Khatian No. 188 was ultimately prepared in their names. 

 11. While said defendants were thus owners in possession of said 23 decimals of land, they transferred 12 decimals to Didarul Islam, Zahurul Islam and Nazrul Islam by three registered deeds being No. 1902, 1903 and 1904 dated 18-4-93 and delivered possession. Said Islam brothers jointly got the land mutated in their names in BS Mutation case No. 3184/92-93 and got BS Khatian No. 188/1 prepared and possessed on payment of rent up to 1403 BS. Then, said Islam brothers transferred their entire purchased land of 12 decimals to the plaintiff by a registered deed being No. 6560 dated 9-11-96 and delivered possession of said 12 decimals and excess land. The plaintiff got the land mutated in his name in said BS Khatian No. 188/1 in mutation case No. 2805/96-97. Accordingly, the plaintiff paid rent up to 1408 BS. The plaintiff has a semi-pucca house wherein a guard lives. He also obtained electric line to the house and an approval of a plan for construction of a commercial building thereupon. 

 12. Further plaintiff’s case is when said defendants purchased 23 decimals and got PS Khatian No. 426/1 recorded, accordingly. Thereafter, BS Khatian No. 188 prepared in the names of the defendants appears to comprise of 27.69 decimals of land. The defendants already got a plan approved for construction of a multi-storied commercial building upon said land of 27.69 decimals. The plaintiff claims to be entitled to a proportionate share of the land, which the defendants possess in excess to their 23 decimals of land. 

 14. Defendants opposed the application. They contended that in 1993 aforesaid Islam brothers purchased 12 decimals of land from them, which they possessed as separate holding and ultimately, in 1996 transferred to the plaintiff by aforesaid deeds with well demarcation and specification by boundary walls. The plaintiff also possessed his purchased land as a separate holding paying rent in separate Khatian. The plaintiff has got no right in law to restrain them from construction. They have also contended that they already spent more than Taka 1 crore in construction of a 9-storied building basement and ground floor were already complete. Materials namely, MS rod, sand, cements, wood, etc. of the value of more than 15 lakh were lying in the site and if the work was suspended they would suffer irreparable loss and injury. They also wanted to continue the construction at their risk and responsibility on condition to hand over vacant possession at his cost of any land covered by construction to the plaintiff if he ultimately succeeds to get in his share in the suit. 

 15. In order to appreciate the case of the plaintiff, we have stated the facts in detail. There is no dispute between the parties about successive sales by the documents mentioned hereinabove. Originally, there were 34 decimals of land in RS Plot No. 2702 of which 11 decimals was acquired in 1963. Plot No. 2701 which is contiguous north of suit plot of 2702 now records 11 decimals. In 1974, defendants purchased the rest of 23 decimals of land from Kala Miah. In 1993 defendants transferred 12 decimals to Didarul Islam and his two brothers by three deeds as mentioned above and in 1996 said Islam Brothers jointly transferred said land to the plaintiffs. It is also not disputed that Islam brothers possessed said land on payment of rents in separate Khatian No. 188/1 and the plaintiff also possesses the same land on payment of rent in the same Khatian by mutation of his name. 

 16. BS Khatian No. 188 prepared in the names of defendants appears to have recorded 27.69 decimals instead of 23 decimals. Plaintiff says that defendant No. 1 encroached upon plot No. 2701 and got said 4.69 decimals recorded in excess to what he  was entitled to in BS Khatian No. 188. The plaintiff then claims that the defendants cannot claim more than 23 decimals and they must share the excess land with him in partition. Accordingly, he avers that Islam brothers delivered possession of 12 decimals plus excess although he did not say what was the quantum of excess. Mr Bhuiyan drew our attention to the deeds of the Islam brothers and also that of the plaintiff to show that Didarul Islam and his bothers purchased 12 decimals of land only and possessed with well demarcation and specification with boundary walls in separate holding, which they transferred to the plaintiff. Plaintiff also possesses very same land in separate holding. Photos of the site have also been annexed to show us how the land of the plaintiff is well bounded. Mr Bhuiyan submitted that the claim of the plaintiff was mala fide, imaginary and baseless and was actuated to obstruct the defendants from making any construction in their land. 

 17. We find recording of 4.69 decimals in excess to 23 decimals in BS Khatian No. 188 has given rise to the claim of the plaintiff and the crux of the dispute. We further find in paragraph 4 of the plaint the plaintiff has categorically averred that he got possession of 6 Gondas in local measurement which is equivalent to 12 decimals plus excess land. Whatever amendment made of the plaint dated 28-11-2001 has not replaced this positive case of the plaintiff. Deed No. 1902 to 1904 dated 18-4-93 and Deed No. 6560 dated 9-11-96 and mutated Khatian No. 188/1 standing in the name of the plaintiff clearly belies the case of the plaintiff that he purchased and got possession of any land in excess of 12 decimals. Now, further question is, if any land is found to have added to the land held by the defendants after his sale of 12 decimals to Didarul Islam and his brothers either by encroachment or otherwise, can the plaintiff lay any valid claim upon such excess land even when he purchased 12 decimals only from Didarul Islam and his brothers. Simple answer is no.
